title: TikTok Account Types: Personal, Business, and Organization
summary: Compare TikTok Personal, Business, and Organization Accounts, understand creator tools and music access, and choose the right setup for your goals.
body_markdown:
## TikTok's current account types


The right choice depends on who owns the profile, what it publishes, how music will be used, and whether multiple people need controlled access. TikTok's[official account-type guide](https://support.tiktok.com/en/using-tiktok/growing-your-audience/switching-to-a-creator-or-business-account) is the authority for the options and feature availability shown in your market.


### Personal Account


A Personal Account is designed for general users and is TikTok's recommended choice for content creators and most public figures. It can use creator tools, may access monetization programs when eligible, and can be set to private. Personal Accounts can access the general music library and the Commercial Music Library, but commercial posts still require the appropriate music rights.


### Business Account


A Business Account is a public profile for a brand, retailer, service company, or other commercial entity. It provides business-focused tools and uses the Commercial Music Library rather than TikTok's general music library. This distinction matters for teams whose posts promote products or services. Website-link and other features depend on TikTok's current eligibility and regional rules.


### Organization Account


An Organization Account is intended for verified organizations that need the account to remain an organizational asset instead of depending on one person's login. TikTok's[Organization Account documentation](https://ads.tiktok.com/help/article/about-organization-accounts) describes role-based permissions, multi-user access, and centralized control. Setup and feature availability vary by market and business platform; TikTok also publishes a separate[Business Center setup guide](https://ads.tiktok.com/help/article/how-to-create-an-organization-account-in-business-center) .
